sources.effective_version: October 13 Chapter 447 was fully read on the General Court website, including 447:5, 6, 8, 9, 10, 12-a and 12-b. Its RSA index states current through the 2026 regular session, updated September 2026; official bound volumes were not read. Listed LSA links stop at 2023; no completed independent 2025-2026 bill search is claimed. Complete primary opinions were read: Boulia-Gorrell, 84 N.H. 174 (1929), Tolles-Bickford, 98 N.H. 55 (1953), and official In re McLaughlin, 2011 BNH 005. Boulia II supports one indivisible entire-contract lien preserved by furnishing within the historical 90-day attachment period; III discusses a possible separate extra-contract claim without deciding its facts. McLaughlin p6 describes 120 days after contractual completion, distinct from accrual; pp8-9 decide first-delivery priority while assuming perfection. Tolles rejects replacement-work and receivership extensions after contractual completion under historical 90 days. These reads supersede blanket case-unread/no-authority wording. CAP OCR confidence is 0.572 (Boulia) and 0.609 (Tolles); printed reporters, full historical amendments and current treatment remain unchecked. Contract identity, qualifying completion and attachment procedure remain qualified. Existing first-delivery +120 conservative review treatment is retained pending bounded product correction; it is not universal statutory expiration. Detailed holdings and limitations are in the bound note. No arithmetic, source-window, guard or approval changes.

sources.effective_version: October 13 Chapter 447 was fully read on the General Court website, including 447:5, 6, 8, 9, 10, 12-a and 12-b. Its RSA index states current through the 2026 regular session, updated September 2026; official bound volumes were not read. Listed LSA links stop at 2023; no completed independent 2025-2026 bill search is claimed. Complete primary opinions were read: Boulia-Gorrell, 84 N.H. 174 (1929), Tolles-Bickford, 98 N.H. 55 (1953), and official In re McLaughlin, 2011 BNH 005. Boulia II supports one indivisible entire-contract lien preserved by furnishing within the historical 90-day attachment period; III discusses a possible separate extra-contract claim without deciding its facts. McLaughlin p6 describes 120 days after contractual completion, distinct from accrual; pp8-9 decide first-delivery priority while assuming perfection. Tolles rejects replacement-work and receivership extensions after contractual completion under historical 90 days. These reads supersede blanket case-unread/no-authority wording. CAP OCR confidence is 0.572 (Boulia) and 0.609 (Tolles); printed reporters, full historical amendments and current treatment remain unchecked. Contract identity, qualifying completion and attachment procedure remain qualified. Existing first-delivery +120 conservative review treatment is retained pending bounded product correction; it is not universal statutory expiration. Detailed holdings and limitations are in the bound note. No arithmetic, source-window, guard or approval changes.

This is court attachment, not recorder filing. Start well before the target; RSA 511-A procedure remains unread. The October 13 reads include Boulia-Gorrell, 84 N.H. 174 (1929), describing an indivisible lien under one entire contract and whole-lien preservation within its historical 90-day period; McLaughlin, 2011 BNH 005, describes the 120-day completion clock but decides priority; Tolles-Bickford, 98 N.H. 55 (1953), rejects completed-contract replacement and receivership extensions. The retained first-delivery +120 date is a conservative review target, not a universal statutory expiration. Contract identity/completion, CAP reporter accuracy and current treatment remain qualified.

After the applicable owner notice, provide written accounts as often as once in thirty days. Late notice protects sums then due or that may thereafter become due to the contractor, agent or subcontractor. Unknown mortgage/posting facts require review; do not omit lender notice.

recurring_notice_intake.label: Actual owner notice and written accounts
recurring_notice_intake.help: Enter actual written accounts and establish the separate actual owner notice. The latest actual act plus thirty days is an advisory checkpoint only; later accounts do not establish timely earlier coverage or a legal cadence reset.

preliminary_notice.name: Owner and construction lender notices
preliminary_notice.description: Give written owner notice before first delivery.

notice_duties.name: Owner notice before furnishing
notice_duties.description: Give written notice to the owner or person having charge of the property before first furnishing. A later notice has the unpaid-balance limitations in RSA 447:6; preserve the existing late-notice and balance review path.

recurring_notice_checkpoints.name: Written-account check-in
recurring_notice_checkpoints.description: Account check-ins are advisory, not settled RSA 447:8 deadlines. Earlier uncovered or late periods remain unresolved; a later logged account does not cure them, reset a legal cadence or establish legal service.

lien_filing.name: Secure lien by writ of attachment
lien_filing.description: Each delivery has its own 120-day window. Secure by attachment by FIRST delivery plus 120; last-delivery candidate is information only and cannot extend earlier deliveries. Conservative action date shown; the statutory deadline remains unresolved. Obtain qualified review before this date.

sources.effective_version: October 13 Chapter 447 was fully read on the General Court website, including 447:5, 6, 8, 9, 10, 12-a and 12-b. Its RSA index states current through the 2026 regular session, updated September 2026; official bound volumes were not read. Boulia II supports one indivisible entire-contract lien preserved by furnishing within the historical 90-day attachment period; III discusses a possible separate extra-contract claim without deciding its facts. McLaughlin p6 describes 120 days after contractual completion, distinct from accrual; pp8-9 decide first-delivery priority while assuming perfection. Tolles rejects replacement-work and receivership extensions after contractual completion under historical 90 days. These reads supersede blanket case-unread/no-authority wording. CAP OCR confidence is 0.572 (Boulia) and 0.609 (Tolles); printed reporters, full historical amendments and current treatment remain unchecked. Contract identity, qualifying completion and attachment procedure remain qualified. Existing first-delivery +120 conservative review treatment is retained pending bounded product correction; it is not universal statutory expiration. Detailed holdings and limitations are in the bound note. No arithmetic, source-window, guard or approval changes.

lien_filing.name: Secure lien by writ of attachment
lien_filing.description: Each delivery has its own 120-day window. Secure by attachment by FIRST delivery plus 120; last-delivery candidate is information only and cannot extend earlier deliveries. Conservative action date shown; the statutory deadline remains unresolved. Obtain qualified review before this date.

sources.effective_version: October 13 Chapter 447 was fully read on the General Court website, including 447:5, 6, 8, 9, 10, 12-a and 12-b. Its RSA index states current through the 2026 regular session, updated September 2026; official bound volumes were not read. Listed LSA links stop at 2023; no completed independent 2025-2026 bill search is claimed. Complete primary opinions were read: Boulia-Gorrell, 84 N.H. 174 (1929), Tolles-Bickford, 98 N.H. 55 (1953), and official In re McLaughlin, 2011 BNH 005. Boulia II supports one indivisible entire-contract lien preserved by furnishing within the historical 90-day attachment period; III discusses a possible separate extra-contract claim without deciding its facts. McLaughlin p6 describes 120 days after contractual completion, distinct from accrual; pp8-9 decide first-delivery priority while assuming perfection. Tolles rejects replacement-work and receivership extensions after contractual completion under historical 90 days. These reads supersede blanket case-unread/no-authority wording. CAP OCR confidence is 0.572 (Boulia) and 0.609 (Tolles); printed reporters, full historical amendments and current treatment remain unchecked. Contract identity, qualifying completion and attachment procedure remain qualified. Existing first-delivery +120 conservative review treatment is retained pending bounded product correction; it is not universal statutory expiration. Detailed holdings and limitations are in the bound note. No arithmetic, source-window, guard or approval changes.

October 13 complete Chapter 447 read and the General Court online compilation statement supersede the original access limitation. The website states currency through the 2026 regular session, updated September 2026, but identifies Thomson Reuters bound volumes/supplements as the official version. Specific procedure, interpretation and appointment limits remain.
Additional service, recording and amount conditions described below remain mandatory; this calculator is not a notice-sending or lien-filing service.

This is court attachment, not recorder filing. Start well before the target; RSA 511-A procedure remains unread. The October 13 reads include Boulia-Gorrell, 84 N.H. 174 (1929), describing an indivisible lien under one entire contract and whole-lien preservation within its historical 90-day period; McLaughlin, 2011 BNH 005, describes the 120-day completion clock but decides priority; Tolles-Bickford, 98 N.H. 55 (1953), rejects completed-contract replacement and receivership extensions. The retained first-delivery +120 date is a conservative review target, not a universal statutory expiration. Contract identity/completion, CAP reporter accuracy and current treatment remain qualified.

After the applicable owner notice, provide written accounts as often as once in thirty days. Late notice protects sums then due or that may thereafter become due to the contractor, agent or subcontractor. Unknown mortgage/posting facts require review; do not omit lender notice.

The General Court website states currency through the 2026 regular session, updated September 2026. Its displayed LSA links stop at 2023; no separate 2025–2026 bill/LSA search or bound official-edition review is recorded here. Retain the existing targeted election/Thanksgiving evidence and attachment-procedure limits.

Account check-ins are advisory, not settled RSA 447:8 deadlines. Earlier uncovered or late periods remain unresolved; a later logged account does not cure them, reset a legal cadence or establish legal service.
A conservative action date is a planning target under an unresolved legal interpretation, not a settled statutory deadline. Obtain qualified review before that date.
Raw candidate dates are not definitive filing deadlines. Calendar adjustments require the cited policy; service, recording cutoffs and compliance still require the applicable facts.

sources.effective_version: October 13 Chapter 447 was fully read on the General Court website, including 447:5, 6, 8, 9, 10, 12-a and 12-b. Its RSA index states current through the 2026 regular session, updated September 2026; official bound volumes were not read. Listed LSA links stop at 2023; no completed independent 2025-2026 bill search is claimed. Complete primary opinions were read: Boulia-Gorrell, 84 N.H. 174 (1929), Tolles-Bickford, 98 N.H. 55 (1953), and official In re McLaughlin, 2011 BNH 005. Boulia II supports one indivisible entire-contract lien preserved by furnishing within the historical 90-day attachment period; III discusses a possible separate extra-contract claim without deciding its facts. McLaughlin p6 describes 120 days after contractual completion, distinct from accrual; pp8-9 decide first-delivery priority while assuming perfection. Tolles rejects replacement-work and receivership extensions after contractual completion under historical 90 days. These reads supersede blanket case-unread/no-authority wording. CAP OCR confidence is 0.572 (Boulia) and 0.609 (Tolles); printed reporters, full historical amendments and current treatment remain unchecked. Contract identity, qualifying completion and attachment procedure remain qualified. Existing first-delivery +120 conservative review treatment is retained pending bounded product correction; it is not universal statutory expiration. Detailed holdings and limitations are in the bound note. No arithmetic, source-window, guard or approval changes.

sources.effective_version: October 13 Chapter 447 was fully read on the General Court website, including 447:5, 6, 8, 9, 10, 12-a and 12-b. Its RSA index states current through the 2026 regular session, updated September 2026; official bound volumes were not read. Listed LSA links stop at 2023; no completed independent 2025-2026 bill search is claimed. Complete primary opinions were read: Boulia-Gorrell, 84 N.H. 174 (1929), Tolles-Bickford, 98 N.H. 55 (1953), and official In re McLaughlin, 2011 BNH 005. Boulia II supports one indivisible entire-contract lien preserved by furnishing within the historical 90-day attachment period; III discusses a possible separate extra-contract claim without deciding its facts. McLaughlin p6 describes 120 days after contractual completion, distinct from accrual; pp8-9 decide first-delivery priority while assuming perfection. Tolles rejects replacement-work and receivership extensions after contractual completion under historical 90 days. These reads supersede blanket case-unread/no-authority wording. CAP OCR confidence is 0.572 (Boulia) and 0.609 (Tolles); printed reporters, full historical amendments and current treatment remain unchecked. Contract identity, qualifying completion and attachment procedure remain qualified. Existing first-delivery +120 conservative review treatment is retained pending bounded product correction; it is not universal statutory expiration. Detailed holdings and limitations are in the bound note. No arithmetic, source-window, guard or approval changes.

Additional service, recording and amount conditions described below remain mandatory; this calculator is not a notice-sending or lien-filing service.

This is court attachment, not recorder filing. Start well before the target; RSA 511-A procedure remains unread. The October 13 reads include Boulia-Gorrell, 84 N.H. 174 (1929), describing an indivisible lien under one entire contract and whole-lien preservation within its historical 90-day period; McLaughlin, 2011 BNH 005, describes the 120-day completion clock but decides priority; Tolles-Bickford, 98 N.H. 55 (1953), rejects completed-contract replacement and receivership extensions. The retained first-delivery +120 date is a conservative review target, not a universal statutory expiration. Contract identity/completion, CAP reporter accuracy and current treatment remain qualified.

After the applicable owner notice, provide written accounts as often as once in thirty days. Late notice protects sums then due or that may thereafter become due to the contractor, agent or subcontractor. Unknown mortgage/posting facts require review; do not omit lender notice.
